# Battlefield 1942 RFA archive format (verified)

Re-derived and machine-validated on 2026-09-23 against **every** `.rfa` in the
`bf_pablov_mod` tree: 814 archives, 448,127 entries, **99.99% structurally
consistent**. All multi-byte integers are little-endian.

## File layout

| Offset | Size | Field |
|--------|------|-------|
| 0      | 4    | `directoryOffset` (u32) — where the file table starts |
| 4      | 4    | `version` (u32) — `0` or `1`; **does not** select the payload layout |
| 8      | ...  | file data blocks |
| `directoryOffset` | ... | directory (file table), which runs to EOF |

There is a fixed 148-byte region before the first data block, so the first block sits at
offset 156. No entry references it and **no reader needs it** — an archive whose data
starts at offset 8 is read correctly by the original `rfaUnpack.exe`. Its content is
producer-specific (identical across `rfaPack.exe` output and several shipped DICE
archives; the Forgotten Hope archive differs) and its meaning is unknown. We reproduce
the exact bytes `rfaPack.exe` writes (`rfa/RfaStamp.h`, generated by
`tools/rfa_stamp_gen.py`) so our archives are structurally indistinguishable from the
tool's, and an in-place `-u` update must preserve the target's existing bytes here rather
than overwrite them.

## Directory

```
u32 numFiles
numFiles x entry
u32 0            (4-byte terminator)
```

### Entry

```
u32 nameLen              // EXACT length of the name; there is NO null terminator
char[nameLen] name       // e.g. "bf1942/levels/Battle_Of_Pavlov-1942/Init.con"
u32 storedSize           // bytes occupied by this entry's data block
u32 uncompressedSize     // size after decompression
u32 dataOffset           // absolute offset of this entry's data block
u32 reserved             // 0 in the archives observed so far
u32 reserved             // 0 in the archives observed so far
u32 flags                // PER-ENTRY, not an archive constant (see below)
```

## Payload layout — two variants

The variant is decided **per entry** from the table, *not* from `version`:

### Raw (no block header)

Condition: `storedSize == uncompressedSize`, or `uncompressedSize == 0`
(which stores 4 bytes).

```
byte[storedSize] payload        // at dataOffset, the verbatim file bytes
```

Observed: 34,617 entries — 34,382 in `version 0` archives but also **235 inside
`version 1` archives**, so version is not a reliable discriminator. Decide
structurally, from the sizes.

### Chunked / LZO1X

Condition: `storedSize != uncompressedSize` and `uncompressedSize != 0`
(413,510 entries — the common case).

```
u32 chunkCount
u32 chunk[0].compressedSize
u32 chunk[0].uncompressedSize
u32 chunk[0].payloadOffset      // always 0
(chunkCount - 1) x {
    u32 compressedSize
    u32 uncompressedSize
    u32 payloadOffset           // running sum of the preceding compressedSize values
}
byte[sum(compressedSize)] payload   // chunks concatenated, in order
```

Invariants, all machine-verified:

* `chunkCount == ceil(uncompressedSize / 32768)` — chunks are **32 KiB**
  (`0x8000`); every chunk except the last has `uncompressedSize == 32768`.
* `storedSize == 16 + 12 * (chunkCount - 1) + sum(compressedSize)`
* `sum(chunk.uncompressedSize) == entry.uncompressedSize`
* `payloadOffset[i] == sum(compressedSize[0..i-1])`
* each chunk is an **LZO1X stream** iff `compressedSize != uncompressedSize`; a chunk
  with `compressedSize == uncompressedSize` is stored verbatim
* `compressedSize` may exceed `uncompressedSize` for incompressible chunks

> ⚠️ The test is **inequality, not less-than**. LZO1X output is frequently *larger* than its
> input — a 1-byte file becomes a 5-byte chunk, and 32 KiB of incompressible data grows
> slightly — so `compressedSize < uncompressedSize` misclassifies exactly the incompressible
> chunks that both the game and `rfaPack.exe` write. Treating such a chunk as verbatim
> returns compressed bytes as though they were file content, which is silent corruption.
> Found by the writer tests, not by review, after an earlier revision of this document had
> stated the wrong rule.

> ⚠️ Earlier revisions of this document described the 16-byte prefix as a constant
> `tag == 1` sub-header holding one payload. That was wrong on both counts: the
> first field is the **chunk count**, and the descriptor table grows by 12 bytes
> per additional chunk. The error is invisible on single-chunk entries — which is
> exactly what the small fixture archives contain, so it survived several passes.

Compression is **LZO1X** (Oberhumer LZO1X-1, as implemented by miniLZO's
`lzo1x_1_compress` / `lzo1x_decompress`). It is NOT zlib/deflate, NOT FastLZ and
NOT RefPack — 7-Zip and .NET `DeflateStream` fail on it.

Verified: packing incompressible N-byte input with `rfaPack.exe -Compress` yields a
single chunk with `compressedSize == N + 4`, whose payload starts with the LZO1X
literal-run byte `N + 17`. LZO1X streams are stateless apart from a caller-supplied
work buffer, and chunks are independent of one another — so both compression and
decompression parallelise cleanly **per chunk**, which is finer-grained than
per file.

## Which variant does a producer choose?

Established by probing `rfaPack.exe` (RFA Pack 1.7) directly:

| Invocation | `version` | entries |
|---|---|---|
| `rfaPack.exe <dir> <base> <out.rfa>` | `0` | all **raw** (`storedSize == uncompressedSize`) |
| `rfaPack.exe <dir> <base> <out.rfa> -Compress` | `1` | all **chunked** |

Mixing the two is what breaks the original tool: a version-1 archive holding a raw,
non-empty entry makes `rfaUnpack.exe` print `ERROR! CRASH  Decompression()!` and extract
nothing for that entry. 235 such entries exist in real archives (mostly the
`bf_1942_kwg_mod` tree) — a producer defect that this reader handles correctly but that a
writer must never create.

## Entry order

Entries are **not** sorted by full path. Each directory contributes its own regular files
(sorted by name) first, and only then its subdirectories (sorted by name), recursively:

```
menu/a.txt  menu/z.txt  menu/d1/c.txt  menu/d1/e/f.txt  menu/d2/b.txt  menu/d3/g.txt
```

ASCII-ascending order would put `menu/z.txt` last. The order reaches the archive table
verbatim, so it must be reproduced exactly for byte-identical output.

## The three encodings of an empty file

| Producer | Encoding |
|---|---|
| `rfaPack.exe` (no `-Compress`) | `storedSize == uncompressedSize == 0` |
| `rfaPack.exe -Compress` | chunked, `chunkCount 1`, `compressedSize 4`, `uncompressedSize 0` |
| shipped DICE archives | `storedSize == 4`, `uncompressedSize == 0` |

All three mean "zero bytes", and `uncompressedSize == 0` is the only reliable signal. The
`-Compress` form is **not** a valid LZO1X stream: miniLZO emits 3 bytes where the 2003-era
LZO emitted 4, and `lzo1x_decompress_safe` rejects the extra byte with
`LZO_E_INPUT_NOT_CONSUMED`. Readers must return zero bytes without consulting the codec —
there is nothing to decompress and nothing to verify.

## Facts used when repacking

* `flags` is **per-entry and varies inside a single archive**: a real FH archive
  held 246 entries with `0xFFFFFFFF` and 5 with `0x7C001CD8`. The `0x028A0220`
  quoted in older notes is a misreading of `0x7C001CD8`. Further values observed:
  `0x77FCB6DE`, `0x00000000`. `rfaPack.exe` writes `0` for new archives and the
  engine still loads them — treat this field as opaque.
  ⚠️ The original `rfaPack.exe -u` **zeroes this field on every entry** rather than
  preserving it (probed with patched archives — see `PLAN_rfa_tools.md` §2.5), so any
  archive it has updated has lost the distinction. Preserving the target's value is
  therefore both safe and a deliberate divergence from the original.
* Entries are ordered by **directory walk, not by full path**: each directory
  contributes its own files (sorted by name) and only then its subdirectories (sorted
  by name), recursively. A full-path sort agrees on flat archives and diverges on
  nested ones, so it must not be used to reproduce an archive.
* The directory terminator (u32 `0` after the last entry) is always zero, and the
  table runs to EOF.
* Use `rfaPack.exe` (with `-Compress`) to build archives. `scripts/list_rfa.ps1`
  and `tools/rfa_probe.py` read the table without decompressing.
* Entries with `uncompressedSize == 0` store 4 bytes and were excluded from the
  structural validation above — confirm their contents before writing them.
